findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when the file is missing, unreadable, or invalid UTF-8
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, MetricsError> and use .map_err(|e| MetricsError::Io(e))

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked index accesses on a Vec that may have fewer than 2 elements
findings.failure_mode: malformed or short lines (e.g. empty file lines, single-field lines) panic with IndexOutOfBounds
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1).ok_or(MetricsError::Invalid) instead of bracket indexing

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() combines unchecked indexing with unwrap on fallible parse
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV lines (missing second field or non-numeric value) panic instead of returning a typed parse/invalid error
findings.fix: use parts.get(1).ok_or(MetricsError::Invalid) then .map_err(|_| MetricsError::Parse) with bounded conversion

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 is a lossy cast: any u32 value above 65535 truncates silently
findings.failure_mode: invalid u16-range values silently wrap instead of returning a domain rejection error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| MetricsError::OutOfRange) after parsing, never 'as'

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is side-effecting I/O embedded in data-parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: pure data loading leaks logging into the core, making the function non-deterministic, non-testable, and violating Data/Calculations/Actions separation
findings.fix: remove println entirely; if metrics are needed, push them to a logging/metrics call at the shell boundary outside the pure parsing closure

findings.problem: raw String primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates intermediate Vec instead of using split_once
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct invalid domain states (empty names, out-of-range values) because no smart constructor validates invariants at parse time
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(MetricsError::Invalid) to extract (_name, value_str), parse value_str with fallible typed conversion, and validate name is non-empty before constructing Record

findings.problem: Record uses pub name: String and pub value: u16 — raw primitives expose domain invariants externally
findings.failure_mode: any caller can create Record with empty name, negative-adjacent values (if i16), or out-of-range u16 values, making illegal states representable
findings.fix: use newtypes like RecordName(String) with a smart constructor that rejects empty/whitespace, and keep value: u16 behind a constructor that validates 0..=65535 via try_from

findings.problem: load_metrics fuses file I/O, CSV parsing, validation, and domain construction into one function returning Vec<Record> with no typed error type
findings.failure_mode: all failure modes (IO error, invalid CSV, parse failure, out-of-range value, empty input) collapse into panic, giving callers zero ability to handle any failure gracefully
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, MetricsError> with an enum { Io(io::Error), Invalid, Parse, OutOfRange, Allocation } and split shell (I/O) from pure parsing at a parse_boundary function

findings.problem: No domain cap on maximum rows, no try_reserve, no bounded allocation — arbitrary file length drives unbounded heap allocation
findings.failure_mode: a sufficiently large file triggers OOM or allocation failure with no graceful degradation
findings.fix: validate a domain cap (max_rows: usize) first, allocate Vec::new(), call out.try_reserve(max_rows).map_err(|_| MetricsError::Allocation)?, enforce max before each push

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_metrics or any performance claim
findings.failure_mode: unknown allocation profile, unknown hot-path behavior, no baseline to validate improvements against
findings.fix: add criterion or similar benchmarks measuring allocations (via alloc_count or similar), throughput (records/sec), and tail latency with representative input distributions

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_metrics allocation and throughput
no profiler data for hot-path analysis
no allocation budget or try_reserve usage in production source
no second-ring evidence (no release provenance, no SIMD/zero-copy claims but also no measurable baseline)
no command evidence: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo test not run in review-only mode
residual_risk: Static review only — no commands executed.
